description_en: Constructed in 1664 CE (NS 784) by a group led by Bhavānīśaṅkara of Kirtipur, the main statue of this temple was established by Bhavānīdāsa. A procession of Kālikā and Bhairava is taken out every year on the 1st of the bright fortnight of Caitra.Standing in the middle of the Kisipiḍi settlement, also known as Kipulcā, this two-story temple has a tiled roof with a balconied tower (phucā) on top. The tower has copper sheets laid on the roof, crowned with a metallic finial bearing an oblong banner (patāḥ) that hangs from the finial down to the temple’s first floor. The struts, which appear to be fairly new, are carved with figures of various deities. The only entrance, facing north, is surmounted by atoraṇafeaturing Kālikā (Cāmuṇḍā) as the central deity. A pair of stone lions guard the main entrance on the outside. The temple’s sanctum, on the upper floor, houses metallic facial sculptures of various mother goddesses, with Kālikā as the temple’s main deity. A pond can be seen in front of the temple, with a smallśivaliṅgato the southeast and statues of Sarasvatī and Umāmaheśvara to the east. Pruscha (1975, p. 266) asserts that there are statues of Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara, Indrāyaṇī, Mahākāla, and Bhagavatī inside the temple.An influential government officer from Kirtipur, Bhavānīdāsa Bhāro, was instrumental in building this temple. Bhavānīśaṅkara, son of Bhavānīdāsa Bhāro, together with other individuals, constructed the temple in 1664 CE (NS 784). Bhavānīdāsa Bhāro, on the other hand, installed the sculptures of the deities and donated land parcels to set up religious trusts (guthi) to oversee daily and periodic rituals at the temple (D. Vajrācārya, VS 2056, p. 133-134). A few years after the temple’s construction, Jayarāma, Śivadāsa, and others offered a gilded flag to the temple, while also installing a brass finial. Another inscription (see ‘historical events’) records the installation of the gilded finial for the deities enshrined in the temple. As the sanctum was inaccessible for this documentation, it was not possible to determine the current status of these finials.The temple underwent renovation in 2003 CE (NS 1123) with government funding and local community involvement. Following damage sustained in the 2015 CE earthquakes, the temple was reconstructed in 2023 CE (VS 2079) with financial support from the Department of Archaeology and Chandragiri Municipality, alongside the active participation of the Gaṇeśa Bhagavatī Kālikā Rājaguthi, a religious trust associated with the temple.The temple priest, a local from the Śreṣṭha caste, conducts daily worship services. Public worship is facilitated for the community on Tuesday and Saturday mornings. On the 1st of the bright fortnight of Caitra, a palanquin procession featuring Kālikā and Bhairava is carried out within the vicinity. This celebration continues for seven days, marked by special worship rituals dedicated to the deities.According to local folklore, the Bhairava residing in the temple originated from Nuwakot and developed a romantic attachment to Kālikā. During one of their frequent encounters, Bhairava experienced a delay in his return. Kālikā, anticipating his predicament, urged him to stay and concealed him within a haystack. The following morning, while tending to his agricultural duties, a farmer stumbled upon Bhairava's hidden presence. Subsequently, the local community intervened, preventing Bhairava's return to Nuwakot, and established his presence within the temple, initiating the tradition of the palanquin procession (local resident, Maharjana, male, age 61).
description_ne: नेसं ७८४ (सन् १६६४) मा कीर्तिपुरका भवानी शंकर सहितको समूहले निर्माण गरेको यस मन्दिरको मूलमूर्ति भवानीदासले राखेका थिए । चैत्रशुक्ल प्रतिपदाका दिन कालिका र भैरवको जात्रा गर्ने परम्परा रहेको छ ।यो मन्दिर किसिपिडि (किपुल्चा) बस्तीको बीचमा अवस्थित छ । बलम्बु र सतुंगल जस्तै किसिपिडि पनि ऐतिहासिक लिच्छविकालीन नेवार बस्ती हो । उत्तराभिमुख दुईतले यस मन्दिरमा झिंगटीको छाना राखिएको छ भने त्यसमाथि फुचा बनाइएको छ । फुचामा भने धातुको छाना माथि धातुकै गजूर चढाइएको छ र गजूरदेखि पहिलो तल्लासम्म आउने गरी धातुको पता: चढाइएको छ । मूलढोकामाथि यस मन्दिरको प्रमुख देवी कालिका (चामुण्डा) केन्द्रमा रहेको काठको तोरण राखिएको छ । पहिलो तलामा रहेको मन्दिरको गर्भगृहमा कालिकालाई प्रमुख बनाई अन्य मातृका देवी र गणहरूको धातुको मुखाकृतिहरू स्थापना गरिएको छ । ढोकाको दायाँ-बायाँ ढुङ्गाका सिंहहरू राखिएका छन् । यहाँ प्रयोग भएका टुँडालहरूमा विभिन्न देवदेवताहरूको आकृति कुँदिएका छन् भने सबै टुँडालहरू नयाँ देखिन्छन् । मन्दिरको ठीक अगाडि (उत्तरमा) एउटा पोखरी रहेको छ । दक्षिणपूर्वमा सानो शिवलिङ्ग र पूर्वमा सरस्वती र उमामहेश्वरको मूर्ति देख्न सकिन्छ । Pruscha (1975, p. 266) ले मन्दिर भित्र पद्मपाणि लोकेश्वर, इन्द्रायणी, महाकाल र भगवतीको मूर्तिहरू रहेको उल्लेख गरेका छन् ।यस मन्दिरको निर्माण नेसं ७८४ (सन् १६६४) मा भएको थियो । मन्दिर बनाउन कीर्तिपुरका भवानीदास भारोको प्रमुख भूमिका रहेको देखिन्छ । उनी त्यस समयका प्रभावशाली व्यक्ति थिए । उनका छोरा भवानी शकर, दुवार समूह र देश समूह मिली मन्दिरको निर्माण गरेको तथ्य मन्दिरमा भएको अभिलेखमा उल्लेख रहेको छ । साथै भवानीदासले मन्दिरको मुख्य देवता बनाएको, मन्दिरको नाममा खेत गुठी राखेको र उक्त खेतबाट आउने अम्दानीले मन्दिरमा पूजा गर्नुपर्ने कुरा उल्लेख भएको छ (D. Vajrācārya VS 2056, p. 133-134) । भवानीदासले मन्दिर बनाएको केहि बर्षपछि नेसं ७९२ (सन् १६७१) मा जयराम, शिवदास लगायतको समुहले यहाँ सुनको झण्डा सहित मन्दिरमा पितलको गजूर पनि चढाएका थिए । त्यसैगरी अर्को अभिलेख अनुसार नेसं ९१३ (सन् १७९२) मा मन्दिरका देवताहरूमा सुनको गजूर चढाउने कार्य गरियो । नेपाल सरकारको आर्थिक सहयोग र स्थानीयको सहभागितामा नेसं ११२३ (सन् २००३) मा मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो । विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पले मन्दिरमा क्षति पुर्‍याएको थियो । पुरातत्त्व विभागको आर्थिक र प्रावधिक सहयोग साथै चन्द्रागिरि नगरपालिकाको आर्थिक सहयोग र श्री गणेश भगवती कालिका राजगुठीको सक्रिय भूमिकामा विसं २०७९ (सन् २०२३) मा मन्दिरको पुनर्निर्माण कार्य सम्पन्न भएको थियो ।मन्दिरको पुजारी श्रेष्ठ थरका स्थानीय रहेको छ । पुजारीले मन्दिरमा दैनिक पूजा गर्दै आइरहेका छन् । स्थानीयलाई हप्ताको दुई दिन (मंगलवार र शनिवार) मन्दिरमा पूजा गर्न बिहान खुला राखिन्छ । घोडे जात्राको समय यस क्षेत्रमा कालिका देवी र भैरवको जात्रा हुने गर्दछ । विशेष पूजाआजा र आराधना गरी सात दिनसम्म मनाउने जात्रामा चैत्रशुक्ल प्रतिपदाको दिन कालिका देवी र भैरवको खट नचाई बस्तीको परिक्रमा गराइन्छ । स्थानीयले जात्राको अवसरमा इष्टमित्र र आफन्त पाहुना बोलाउने र भोजभतेर गरी जात्रा मनाउने चलन रहेको छ । लोककथन अनुसार यहाँ रहेको भैरव नुवाकोटका थिए । उनी यहाँको कालिका देवीको सुन्दरतामा मोहित भई प्रेममा परेका थिए । सधैंजसो भेटघाट गर्ने क्रममा एकदिन भैरव फर्किन ढिला भएछ । कालिकाले भैरवलाई त्यतै बस्न अनुरोध गरिन् र परालभित्र लुकाएर राखिन् । भोलि बिहान काम गर्ने सिलसिलामा एक किसानले भैरव लुकेर बसेको देखे । त्यसपछि स्थानीय सबैले भैरवलाई नुवाकोट फर्कन नदिई यहीँ स्थापना गरी जात्रा मनाउन थाले (local resident, Maharjana, male, age 61) ।

historical_events.event_description: Bhavānīśaṅkara, son of Bhavānīdāsa Bhāro, from Kirtipur built the temple together with other individuals from local groups named Duvāra and Deśa. Bhavānīdāsa Bhāro, on the other hand, installed the sculptures of the deities and donated land parcels to set religious trusts to oversee daily and periodic rituals at the temple.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of gilded flag and brass finial
historical_events.event_description: Bhavānīdāsa offered a gilded flag to the temple while also installing a brass finial together with Jayarāma, Śivadāsa, and others.

The deities enshrined in the temple received an offering of gilded finials from Phojasi Mahata, Mildārāma, Daśanārāyaṇa, Siddhisiha, Dharmanātha, Maheśvara, Śrīkṛṣṇa, and the chief of a local religious trust.
Rāmacandra of Kipulcā, together with his wife Māyācā, his younger brother Jogalāla and his wife Nanda laid the temple premises with black stone slabs.
The temple underwent renovation with government funding and local community involvement.

Following damage sustained in the 2015 earthquakes, the temple was reconstructed in 2023 CE (VS 2079) with financial support from the Department of Archaeology and Chandragiri Municipality, alongside the active participation of the Gaṇeśa Bhagavatī Kālikā Rājaguthi, a religious trust associated with the temple.
